title: PIL Procedure — Filing, Affidavits, Bona Fides and Maintainability

content.overview: PIL procedure covers how a public-interest claim is filed and screened: forum choice, pleadings or letter-initiation, affidavits, disclosure of bona fides, and threshold maintainability under Articles 32 and 226. Liberal standing does not remove the need for a factual foundation and good faith.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Correct forum (32 or 226)? (2) Clear public injury pleaded? (3) Affidavit and bona fides disclosed? (4) Alternative remedy? (5) Abuse markers?
content.study:
Core rule: Even with liberal standing, the court needs a maintainable petition — identified parties or class, pleaded public injury, supporting material, and bona fide purpose.

Filing routes: Formal writ petition with affidavit, or epistolary initiation later regularised. After registration, ordinary writ process (notice, response, orders) applies.

Bona fides and maintainability: Courts examine credentials, motive, substantial public injury, and absence of personal gain. Vague or private disputes fail at the threshold.

Current-law framing: Articles 32 and 226 plus judicial screening practice. Case-law verification remains separate.

sections.heading: Forum and initiation
sections.body: Choose Article 32 (Supreme Court, Part III) or Article 226 (High Court, fundamental and other legal rights, territorial limits). Initiation may be formal petition or, in fit cases, a screened letter treated as petition.

sections.heading: Pleadings and affidavits
sections.body: Plead the public injury, legal duty, and relief with enough particulars for notice and response. Affidavits support facts; false or reckless allegations invite costs.

sections.heading: Bona fides disclosure
sections.body: Petitioners should disclose interest, funding where relevant, and absence of personal or political collateral purpose. Concealment undermines maintainability.

sections.heading: Threshold maintainability checks
sections.body: Public character of injury, standing, alternative remedy where relevant, vagueness, and abuse filters are applied before full merits hearing.

sections.heading: After registration
sections.body: Notice, counter-affidavits, interim orders, and final relief follow ordinary writ practice. Procedure flexibility at entry does not suspend later process discipline.

examples.title: Incomplete affidavit
examples.body: A PIL alleges systemic pollution without identifying the authority, affected class, or supporting facts on affidavit. The issue is threshold rejection for want of foundation.

examples.title: Hidden private interest
examples.body: Petitioner seeks cancellation of a licence held by a business rival without disclosing the rivalry. The issue is bona fides and possible costs.

hypotheticals.question: Does liberal standing remove the need for affidavits?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Facts still need a sworn foundation; flexibility at initiation does not abolish evidentiary discipline.

distinctions.title: Procedure vs locus standi
distinctions.left: Procedure: how the claim is filed, verified, and screened.
distinctions.right: Standing: who may be heard in public interest.

misconceptions.trap: Any letter automatically becomes a full hearing.
misconceptions.correction: Epistolary initiation is screened; registration and maintainability still apply.

cases.name: State of Uttaranchal v. Balwant Singh Chaufal
cases.facts: The Court addressed misuse of PIL jurisdiction for private or publicity-oriented objectives.
cases.issue: What safeguards prevent abuse of public-interest jurisdiction?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts must verify credentials, motive, substantial public injury and the absence of personal gain before entertaining PIL.
cases.holding: The Court issued guidelines for screening and controlling PIL abuse.
cases.relevance: Primary orientation for procedural screening; verification gate open.

cases.name: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India
cases.facts: Access to constitutional courts and public standing.
cases.issue: When may a person approach for public injury?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Standing may be relaxed for bona fide public redress where the directly affected cannot approach effectively.
cases.relevance: Standing context for procedure; verification gate open.

cases.name: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts may use flexible procedure and continuing directions for effective enforcement.
cases.holding: Petition treated as vehicle for Article 21 enforcement.
cases.relevance: Flexible process orientation; verification gate open.
